method: Every entry below was produced by a command run in this session and is reproducible from the scripts named. Nothing here is an inference presented as a fact; where a statement is a model it is tagged [MODEL].

entries.title: Prior fork assertion contradicted by current GitHub metadata
entries.fact: On 2026-10-06 GitHub API reports fork=false, parent=null for buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE41. The inherited statement that this is currently a public organizer fork is not supported.
entries.why_it_matters: Repository ancestry alone does not determine competition eligibility. No organizer repository is modified by this project.
entries.action_requested: Retain the dated correction; independently review participant eligibility, licenses, and public-solution rules. This is not a legal clearance.
entries.status: CORRECTED — current repository is standalone; broader eligibility not adjudicated

entries.title: The brief's 'highest score' figure is stale
entries.fact: The task brief states 0.3195 is the highest score on the leaderboard. A 2026-10-04 read of the public leaderboard shows 0.3262 (rank 1, nchuzhoy), 0.3222 (rank 2, kinghorton42), 0.3195 (rank 3, DARD).
entries.why_it_matters: Any claim about 'beating the best' must be measured against 0.3262, not 0.3195. Treating 0.3195 as the bar understates the target by 0.0067. All arithmetic in this repository uses 0.3262.
entries.raised_by: independent read; note the brief's number is not wrong, only older

entries.title: The family's 44,090 px anchor is declared defective by its own sibling project
entries.fact: The sibling project GEMSDOE32 declares its shipped `h19-5-smoothmaxcov-44090.tif` defective, and the reference-solution family nonetheless treats a 44,090 px artifact as the incumbent support. The published 0.2600 / 0.2778 scores are attached to artifacts in that lineage.
entries.why_it_matters: If the base artifact is defective then the mass-to-score relationship was measured on a defective base, and conclusions drawn from that lineage (including 'thinning always helps') inherit the defect. This session therefore measures mass behaviour directly on the strand-level holdout instead of extrapolating from the leaderboard lineage.
entries.evidence: evidence/data_manifest.json and the sibling GEMSDOE32 notes; the defect is asserted by that project, not independently re-verified here
entries.status: FLAGGED — mitigated by measuring the mass response in-house

entries.title: Prior H33 causal and metric claims exceeded evidence
entries.fact: The metric is DTI, not its reciprocal. For G truth pixels, 1/DTI = 0.2 + 0.2 FP/TP + 0.8 G/TP. FP is distance-weighted prediction mass; not every emitted pixel adds exactly 0.2. GEMSDOE32 describes H33 as a 200 m prune of a reported 0.2708 base, not simply the 0.2600 file. Its page still labels the artifact unscored.
entries.why_it_matters: Removing redundant mass may help, but pruning can lose coverage of genuine hidden faults. The prior claim of free deletion and organizer masking in both rounds is not established by locally retained primary evidence and is withdrawn. 0.2778 remains user-reported, not tied to an organizer TIFF receipt.
entries.status: CORRECTED — no causal or organizer-masking claim

entries.title: The transfer-corridor hypothesis FAILED three independent tests (honest negative)
entries.fact: (1) Corridor-only emission scores 0.0000 on the strand-level holdout, in 4 of 4 folds and at all 6 settings — reproduced independently by a parallel session. (2) On the 2020 USGS catalogue, 16 events M>=4.0 lie 7.07 to 83.19 px from every mapped fault (0 within 300 m, 11 beyond 3 km). (3) Against 27,092 INGENIOUS well records, the transfer elements are DEPLETED for hot sites (enrichment 0.34x, p=1.0) while the published catalogue is enriched 2.15x at p=0.016 — so the test has power and the corridor fails it.
entries.why_it_matters: This is published as a negative result, not buried. The corridor is where the catalogue is NOT; a hypothesis that is true of the region's geology is not thereby true of the hidden set. Reporting it is the point of the irregularities page.
entries.status: NEGATIVE RESULT — recorded, and the hypothesis is not shipped

entries.title: A unit and mask-order bug made an earlier seismicity artifact wrong
entries.fact: The first publication of `run_seismicity.py` reported a corridor of 0 pixels, then 12,279,160 pixels (a metres-in-pixels unit confusion), then 190,382 px (scatter matrix not normalised by n). The released version measures the minor-axis sigma as a covariance in metres (1,919.5 m) and gives 11,992 px with 11,965 px off-catalogue.
entries.why_it_matters: Two wrong intermediate artifacts existed on disk. Anyone reading a cached copy could have carried the error forward. The check that caught it is the footprint-relative area: a corridor covering 94 % of the footprint cannot be a corridor.
entries.status: FIXED — published artifact is the corrected one

entries.title: The winning criterion is nearly inert at the mass the public leaderboard uses
entries.fact: Rebuilt at the same 2.83 px spacing with the same B=2 catalogue prune, the kinematic ranking shares 94.1 % of its pixels with an uninformative uniform control at 32,151 px. The measured advantage is 1.52x at 2,500 px, 1.30x at 5,000, 1.25x at 20,000 and 1.006x at 30,000 px.
entries.why_it_matters: An artifact built at the family's 37,654 px mass would have looked like a test of this hypothesis while testing almost nothing. The primary artifact was therefore moved to a 20,000 px mass, where the measured ratio is 1.25x, and the dense twin is shipped alongside as its own control.
entries.status: ADDRESSED — primary artifact chosen at a mass where the criterion is measurably active

entries.title: Live leaderboard values could not be re-verified from this sandbox
entries.fact: The sandbox's own network egress cannot reach drivendata.org, usgs.gov or gdr.openei.org by command line; those reads required an external page-fetch tool. Every leaderboard number in this repository is therefore a dated snapshot, not a live reading.
entries.why_it_matters: A score cited as current may have moved. All such numbers are labelled with their read date.
entries.evidence: network probes recorded in the session; registry/score_ledger.csv carries the snapshot date
entries.status: ACKNOWLEDGED — all such figures are date-stamped

entries.title: The projection constant is a MODEL, not a measurement
entries.fact: K_HIDDEN_PX = 13,000 is inferred from an owner-reported score on a hidden set, spanning 12,691 to 15,200 px depending on which member of a three-artifact trio is used.
entries.why_it_matters: Projected scores in this repository are conditional on that constant and are never presented as measurements. Only ratios between two rankers measured on the identical holdout are instrument-internal and therefore comparable across artifacts.

entries.title: `existing_faults.tif` is byte-identical to the label raster in the pinned mirrors (label-provenance trap)
entries.fact: SHA-256 equality (7ba308cc...) between data/existing_faults.tif and the training labels mirror was verified 2026-10-06; sample_submission.tif contains 60,988 ones coincident with label pixels despite 'total fault absence' wording. Either round-1 training labels equal the public catalogue or the mirrors carry an alias.
entries.why_it_matters: Any 'expert-holdout' scored against pixels that are themselves catalogue members, with predictions derived from the same catalogue, is self-referential. This forced the H42-HO design (truth = SGMC residual only, 3 px isolation guard, retained-geometry excluded) and is also why docs/downloads/holdout.json (older H33-lineage instrument) and evidence/h42_holdout.json numbers must NEVER be compared to each other.
entries.action_requested: Organizer-level confirmation of what existing_faults.tif is. No pipeline change: format/grid usage is unaffected.
entries.evidence: research/hypotheses-h42.md Part 6 (its items were renumbered IRR-10..12 here because the registry already had an IRR-09); verified by sha256sum in-session

entries.title: External USGS/GDR endpoints unreachable from the sandbox; all external data came via the GitHub mirror path
entries.fact: mrdata.usgs.gov, gdr.openei.org and other USGS endpoints returned HTTP 000 from this environment (measured 2026-10-06). SGMC and thermal-probe rasters were fetched from the sibling project's CI-derived repo mirrors via `gh api` and digest-checked against the sibling's own receipts.
entries.why_it_matters: Digest equality proves mirror integrity, not organizer authentication of the upstream USGS bytes. The repo's independent 300 m burn matched the sibling receipt exactly (82,151 px footprint; 61,664 off-catalogue >300 m), which cross-validates the mirror but not the USGS publication chain.
entries.action_requested: When network access exists, re-download NV.zip/CA.zip from mrdata.usgs.gov and compare shas (3b333ac0.../78765ba4...) before trusting the SGMC prior further.

entries.title: Sibling `sgmc-off-catalogue-44k` (GEMSDOE29) has no recorded score - idea possibly uploaded, never scored
entries.fact: The owner-reported score ledger lists sgmc-off-catalogue-44k with a blank score. No claim is made that the SGMC idea is leaderboard-untried; the claim is limited to: this construction (bimodal orientation-ranked lattice + corroboration gate + H42-HO validation) does not exist on any audited site.
entries.why_it_matters: Uniqueness and 'new idea' framing must stay narrow: our H42-D artifact's support overlaps the idea-class (44k vs 22,061 px, different ranking and pruning) though not any shipped raster (max Jaccard 0.0118).
entries.action_requested: Owner to check the GEMSDOE29 submissions page manually; repo does not and will not poll DrivenData.

entries.title: Mirror set missing anchor_02600_zeros.tif; scripts/build_final.py cannot be rerun end-to-end
entries.fact: The sibling mirror integrity receipt on this repo's main reports INTEGRITY_OK: false because anchor_02600_zeros.tif is absent. build_final.py consumes that anchor.
entries.why_it_matters: The H41-era artifacts remain valid dated receipts, but they cannot be regenerated by their own builder from this checkout. H42 was built by scripts/run_h42.py, which is fully rerunnable from pinned inputs (verified twice: identical pixel hashes across runs).
entries.action_requested: Do not attempt to 'fix' build_final by substitution. If the anchor is needed, refetch it from the sibling repo path or declare the H41 artifacts immutable history.
entries.evidence: docs/downloads/manifest.json (top-level H41 keys), research/hypotheses-h42.md Part 2 footnote

entries.title: The hidden label count carried in this repository was 2.8x too small
entries.fact: validate.K_HIDDEN_PX = 13,000 was inferred from adjacent pairs of owner-reported scores under the assumption FP_w ~= mass.  Keeping the double-counting term q in the same algebra and fitting 1/score = c0 + m*mass over an exactly nested five-file lineage (containment 1.0000, verified from the bytes) gives rho = 36,467 px, and the eight-point chain gives 35,533 px.
entries.why_it_matters: Every projected score in the repository is conditioned on this constant.  At rho = 36,000 the optimal emitted mass is roughly 3x larger than at rho = 13,000, so the old constant biased every mass recommendation low.
entries.action_requested: Keep both numbers visible.  Do not silently overwrite K_HIDDEN_PX; the new estimate is itself a [MODEL] resting on owner-reported scores.
entries.status: ACKNOWLEDGED -- published as IR-42-RHO-01 in research/score-record-calculus.md

entries.title: The blocked holdout used in every previous session cannot score an off-catalogue candidate
entries.fact: The prize round scores faults absent from the published catalogue and masks catalogue pixels out of every term.  A holdout whose truth IS the published catalogue, with the retained catalogue masked, returns ~0 for any candidate engineered to avoid the catalogue.  H41-A measured 7.098e-09 and H41-E 0.000000 on that instrument.
entries.why_it_matters: Those zeros were read as geological failures.  They are instrument failures.  Decisions taken on them -- including closing the slot gate on H41-A -- rested on a measurement that could not have been nonzero.
entries.action_requested: Use the H-SIM protocol (whole withheld strands as truth, retained catalogue masked, scoring beyond a guard) for every future candidate.  Re-read the H41 zeros as 'not measurable', not as 'zero skill'.

entries.title: 3,061 pixels inside the scoring footprint carry the -3.4e38 nodata sentinel in all 19 bands
entries.fact: training_features.tif encodes nodata as the float32 sentinel -3.4028234663852886e+38.  Measured here: 58,171 band-pixels across the 19 bands, on 3,061 distinct pixels, all of them INSIDE the 5,167,373-pixel scoring footprint (band 6 `tc` carries 3,073).  Band 1's own valid mask is 5,165,852 px, i.e. 1,521 px smaller than the template footprint.
entries.why_it_matters: Any pipeline that reads a feature band without sanitising the sentinel, or that derives the footprint from a feature band instead of from sample_submission.tif, ships illegal values and triggers the portal's 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]' rejection.  This is the mechanism behind the error the owner hit on a downloaded file.
entries.action_requested: Take the footprint only from np.isfinite(sample_submission.tif); sanitise the sentinel per band; re-read the delivered bytes and assert finiteness before offering a file.
entries.status: FIXED -- shipped artifact is all-finite and independently re-verified

entries.title: A 21-template inversion for the hidden label field is not identified by 29 scalar scores
entries.fact: Fitting u = sum_j w_j u_j over 21 geological templates plus rho to all 29 probe scores gives RMSE 0.106 and leave-one-probe-out RMSE 0.111 with systematic residuals: every high scorer is under-predicted and every dense low scorer over-predicted.  A dense probe (516,738 px) has a ~= 0.9 for almost any u while its reported 0.0748 demands a ~= 0.20, and the 0.2778 file demands >= 3.2x concentration inside 6.9% of the domain; no smooth mixture of catalogue distance and single-band anomalies satisfies both.
entries.why_it_matters: It would have been easy to publish a fitted label field from this.  The fit is not identified, so any such field would be an artefact of the basis chosen.
entries.action_requested: Report the failure.  Use only the nested-lineage ratio fit, which never needs u.
entries.status: ACKNOWLEDGED -- published as a negative result

entries.title: dataset_mask().sum() is 255 x footprint, not footprint
entries.fact: For existing_faults.tif and sample_submission.tif, src.dataset_mask().sum() returns 1,317,680,115, which is exactly 255 x 5,167,373.  rasterio returns a uint8 mask with 255 inside, not a boolean.
entries.why_it_matters: A footprint check written as `mask.sum() == FOOTPRINT_PX` fails on a perfectly correct file, and a check written as `(mask>0).sum()` passes.  Earlier session notes recorded this as an unexplained read oddity; it is now explained.
entries.action_requested: Always compare (mask > 0).sum() against the footprint count.
entries.status: RESOLVED -- explained, not an upstream defect
